noticed_not_touched.what: The snapshot match in graphState (`catalog && freshness?.snapshotId === catalog.snapshotId ? freshness : catalog`) is redundant: setCatalog is called in one place (line 393) and is always followed by setFreshness(null) in the same batch, and setFreshness(value) is only called with result.snapshotId === loadedSnapshot.current, which equals the catalog's snapshot. So freshness is either null or of the loaded snapshot, and R2-18 (`freshness ?? catalog`) is an equivalent mutant no input can tell apart. Either drop the guard or drop the setFreshness(null) and keep the guard as the single rule; keeping both is harmless.

If the explorer is hidden and shown again while protocol negotiation is still pending, the `!loaded.current` guard is what keeps the first catalog read loud; without it the visible effect would set quietRead before any read and the first read would be quiet (no error shown on failure). The test added for R2-14 pins the guard through a failed first read instead; the negotiation path is not pinned separately.

assumptions: A wiki-link lookup's own target is remembered by viewInGraph's direct remember(node) call, not by the node-memory effect, so the existing 'Back to a node reached through a lookup' test cannot kill R2-23. The new F-008 test uses a search hit (a lookup through the search field) whose node leaves `nodes` when the search is cleared; that is the path where only the effect fills the memory.
